references.text: Jesus' words that he will soon leave the disciples and go to the Father are repeated almost verbatim in John 13:33, where he says: "Where I am going, you cannot come".

The motif of a short period before Jesus' disappearance and return is central in John 16:16-17, where he asks: "A little while, and you will not see me; and again a little while, and you will see me".
The concept that Jesus "goes" to the one who sent him (the Father) is a recurring theme in John 14:28, where he says: "I am going away and I will come back to you".
The warning that one cannot follow Jesus where he goes, because he is going to another place, is expressed in John 8:21, where he says: "I am going away, and you will seek me and die in your sin".

The prayer text where Jesus asks to be gathered with the Father confirms that he will soon "go" to him, as mentioned in John 17:11: "I am no longer in the world, but they are in the world, and I am coming to you".
